speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām |
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate ||
english: People will tell of your disgrace for ever, and for someone who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam ||
english: The great warriors will think you pulled back from battle out of fear, and those who once thought highly of you will think little of you.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ||
english: Your enemies will say many things that should never be said, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ ||
english: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, resolved to fight.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi ||
english: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, prepare yourself for battle. Then you will incur no sin.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
iast:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu |
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi ||
english: This is the understanding I have taught you in terms of Sankhya. Now hear it in terms of yoga: joined with this understanding, son of Pritha, you will throw off the bondage of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
iast:
nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||
english: On this path no effort is wasted and no harm comes from falling short. Even a little of this practice protects a person from great fear.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
iast:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana |
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām ||
english: On this path, Arjuna, the resolute mind is single-pointed; but the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ |
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ ||
english: The unwise, son of Pritha, who delight in the letter of the Vedas and claim there is nothing more, speak flowery words

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
iast:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām |
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati ||
english: full of desire, intent on heaven, offering rebirth as the reward of action, and crowded with special rites for gaining pleasure and power.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām |
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||
english: Those who cling to pleasure and power, their minds carried away by such words, do not develop the resolute understanding that rests in deep concentration.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
iast:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna |
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān ||
english: The Vedas deal with the three gunas. Rise above the three gunas, Arjuna: be free of the pairs of opposites, always grounded in purity, unconcerned with getting and keeping, and centred in the self.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके ।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
iast:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake |
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ ||
english: As much use as there is in a small well when water is flooding everywhere, so much is there in all the Vedas for a brahmin who truly knows.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi ||
english: Your right is to the work alone, never to its results. Do not let the results be your motive, and do not become attached to doing nothing.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनंजय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
iast:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya |
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||
english: Established in yoga, do your work, Arjuna, giving up attachment and staying the same in success and failure. This evenness of mind is called yoga.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनंजय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanaṃjaya |
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ ||
english: Action done for its results is far inferior to the discipline of understanding, Arjuna. Seek refuge in that understanding; those whose motive is the result are pitiable.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
iast:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam ||
english: One joined with this understanding leaves behind both good and bad deeds, here in this life. So devote yourself to yoga: yoga is skill in action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
iast:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam ||
english: The wise, joined with this understanding, give up the fruit that action brings; freed from the bondage of rebirth, they reach the state beyond all suffering.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
iast:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati |
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca ||
english: When your understanding crosses beyond the thicket of delusion, you will become indifferent to what you have heard and to what you have yet to hear.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi ||
english: When your understanding, unsettled by all you have heard, stands firm and unmoving in deep concentration, then you will attain yoga.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
iast:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim ||
english: Krishna, how would you describe a person of steady wisdom, settled in deep concentration? How does someone of steady mind speak, how do they sit, how do they move?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
iast:
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān |
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate ||
english: Son of Pritha, when a person gives up every desire that enters the mind and is content in the self, by the self, that person is said to be of steady wisdom.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
iast:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ |
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate ||
english: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrows, who does not crave pleasures, and who is free of passion, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham |
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
english: One who is without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices at good fortune nor resents misfortune, has wisdom that is firmly established.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
english: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, a person withdraws the senses completely from their objects, that person's wisdom is firmly established.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
iast:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||
english: When an embodied person stops feeding the senses, their objects fall away, but the taste for them remains; even that taste fades once the supreme is seen.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
iast:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ ||
english: Even when a wise person is striving, son of Kunti, the turbulent senses forcibly carry the mind away.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ |
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
english: Having restrained them all, one should sit disciplined, intent on me. One whose senses are under control has wisdom that is firmly established.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
iast:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate |
saṅgātsaṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate ||
english: When a person dwells on the objects of the senses, attachment to them arises; from attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
iast:
krodhādbhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ |
smṛtibhraṃśādbuddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati ||
english: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confused memory; from confused memory, the loss of reason; and when reason is lost, a person is ruined.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran |
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati ||
english: But one who moves among the objects of the senses with senses free of attraction and aversion, under the self's control, with a disciplined mind, attains inner calm.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
iast:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate |
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ||
english: In that calm, all sorrows come to an end; for the understanding of one whose mind is calm soon becomes steady.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
iast:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ||
english: One who is undisciplined has no understanding and no power of contemplation; without contemplation there is no peace, and without peace, how can there be happiness?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
iast:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nu vidhīyate |
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi ||
english: When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away a person's wisdom, as the wind carries away a boat on the water.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
english: So, mighty-armed one, a person whose senses are completely held back from their objects has wisdom that is firmly established.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||
english: What is night for all beings is the time of waking for the self-controlled; and when other beings are awake, that is night for the sage who truly sees.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
iast:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī ||
english: As waters flow into the ocean, which is always being filled yet stays still within its bounds, so the person into whom all desires flow in this way finds peace; not the one who chases desires.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान् पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvān pumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati ||
english: A person who gives up all desires and lives free of longing, without any sense of 'mine' and without ego, attains peace.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati ||
english: This is the state of Brahman, son of Pritha. Having reached it, a person is never deluded again; remaining in it even at the hour of death, they attain the peace of Brahman.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
iast:
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana |
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava ||
english: Krishna, if you think that understanding is better than action, then why do you urge me into this terrible action?
